channel.title: Academic Jobs on Pieter Belmans
channel.description: Recent content in Academic Jobs on Pieter Belmans

item.title: Postdoc position in algebraic geometry
item.description:
I am excited to announce a postdoc position in algebraic geometry .

The summary:

  • starting date is October 1 2026 (or as soon as possible thereafter)
  • it is for 3 years (with a 1-year probation)
  • the focus is (derived categories of) Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces, so some experience with these or topics closely related to it is required
  • it is part of a joint grant between Andreas Krug and myself, and regular visits to Hannover are anticipated
  • we will start reviewing and interviewing candidates after the application deadline of February 22

There is a really active research group on algebraic geometry in Utrecht, and the Netherlands is a great place in general for algebraic geometry, with many interesting activities.

item.title: An assistant professorship at Utrecht University
item.description:
The previous such post is only a few months old, but here is another position!

Utrecht University is hiring an assistant professor in pure mathematics, not tied to specific area. I can attest it is a great place to work, so if you fit the (broad) profile, and would like to work at Utrecht University, please consider applying!

If you have questions, you can ask me, or in case of more official questions, the head of the committee, which is Gijs Heuts.

item.title: An assistant professorship at Utrecht University
item.description:
Utrecht University is hiring an assistant professor in (arithmetic) algebraic geometry and number theory. I can attest it is a great place to work, so if you fit the (broad) profile, and would like to work at Utrecht University, please consider applying!

If you have questions, you can ask me, or in case of more official questions, the head of the committee, which is Lennart Meier.

item.title: PhD position in algebraic geometry and representation theory
item.description:
Almost a year ago I announced that there were open PhD positions on a Luxembourgish block grant called GRACE, but that at the time we were most likely not hiring anyone in a subject close to my interests. That has now changed, with the updated posting on MathJobs: there is a position available which is supervised jointly by Karin Melnick and myself.

It focuses on the use of representation-theoretic methods in algebraic and differential geometry, e.g., the use of equivariant vector bundles to describe zero loci on homogeneous varieties.

item.title: PhD and postdoc position in algebraic geometry
item.description:
I am excited to announce two ways in which you can join my team:

  • as a postdoc (see also the MathJobs link)
  • as a PhD student

The summary:

  • Both are intended to start between September and January (or as soon as possible thereafter).
  • The postdoc position is a 2-year position (described as 1 + 1 in the official advertisement), with the possibility to extend it to 3 years upon positive evaluation.
    The PhD position is a 4-year position.
  • Both come with small teaching duties.
  • There is a really active research group on algebraic geometry in Utrecht, and the Netherlands is a great place in general for algebraic geometry, with many interesting activities.
  • We will start reviewing and interviewing candidates after the application deadline of July 7.

Both positions are funded by the NWO, through the Vidi project CatsINCAGe, and thus are concerned with noncommutative algebraic geometry, with a focus on Fourier–Mukai transforms, Hochschild cohomology, algebraic stacks, semiorthogonal decompositions, moduli spaces of sheaves:

item.title: PhD positions at the University of Luxembourg
item.description:
The Department of Mathematics at the University of Luxembourg has 8 open positions, as part of a project in fundamental mathematics with a significant computational and experimental twist. All information on how to apply can be found there.

The earliest starting date for any of the positions is late 2024. I do not necessarily plan to fill the position attached to my part of the project as early as possible, spring or summer of 2025 is more likely, but you can certainly express your interest in working with me.

item.title: Postdoc position in derived algebraic geometry with Sarah Scherotzke
item.description:
My colleague Sarah Scherotzke is advertising a postdoc position in derived algebraic geometry on MathJobs. The focus is on derived algebraic geometry. It is not inconceivable that you get to interact with me too, given that Sarah and I lead a joint research group on algebraic geometry and representation theory.

If you have any questions, you can email her, or both of us (or just me, if you think I'm better placed to answer your question).

item.title: Postdoc position on MathJobs
item.description:
Link to the position. The deadline is January 20.

As explained a bit earlier, I have a postdoc position to work with me. Please spread the news! And if you have any questions, just ask.

item.title: Postdoc position in algebraic geometry / representation theory
item.description:
There's no official posting yet, but here I can make a non-official post.

There is a postdoc position available at the University of Luxembourg, to work with me, funded by my FNR OPEN grant 'AdEMAR' (Admissible Embeddings for Moduli spaces in Algebra and Representation theory).

  • It is to start September 2023 (or as soon as possible thereafter).
  • It is a 2-year position, with the possibility to extend it to 3 years upon positive evaluation.
  • It comes with minor teaching duties (on the order of TA'ing 1 course per semester).
  • It comes with a highly competitive salary, and Belval is a great place to work.
  • There is an active research group on algebraic geometry and representation theory at the University of Luxembourg.

I'm looking for a candidate with a strong background in some of these topics:

item.title: An associate / full professorship at the University of Luxembourg
item.description:
We are hiring a new associate / full professor in mathematics at the University of Luxembourg. It is open to all areas of mathematics, but of course it would be great to strengthen the department with someone with algebraic or geometric interests!

If you have any questions, you can just ask me.

item.title: PhD position at the University of Luxembourg
item.description:
I have a position open for a PhD student, to work in the group formed by Sarah Scherotzke and myself, on derived categories of moduli spaces and links to deformation theory in algebraic geometry and noncommutative algebra.

The position would normally start in the fall of 2022.

To apply, please send me:

  • a letter explaining your background and interests
  • a sample of your mathematical writing (e.g. a chapter of your master thesis)
  • a curriculum vitae and transcript with grades
  • 2 names of reference letter writers (no need to have letters sent to me yet)

item.title: Moving to the University of Luxembourg
item.description:
I am very excited to share the news that I'll be starting as an assistant professor at the University of Luxembourg this summer. I'm really looking forward to start!

Not entirely unrelated to the message above the fold, I'd like to advertise:

  • this postdoc position, associated to Sarah Scherotzke.
  • these 3 PhD positions, which can be taken up with 5 of my future colleagues.

Especially for the postdoc position: in case you wish to work on topics that Sarah Scherotzke is interested in, it could be useful to know that I'll be starting there too, given the overlap between our research interests.

item.title: Starting my postdoc
item.description: A quick update: This week I have started my postdoc at the Max Planck Institute for Mathematics in Bonn. Feel free to come and say hi in office 402.

item.title: Do you want to be my colleague?
item.description: Or rather, do you want to be a PhD student in quadratic form theory at the University of Antwerp? Because I will have left by the time you'd begin, we'd be colleagues for at most 2 months (but that's not why you should apply for this position). In any case, they are looking for one person in algebra.

item.title: Do you want to be my colleague?
item.description: Unlike the previous time there is now a non-teaching PhD position available in the area of quadratic form theory, under Karim Johannes Becher.

item.title: Do you want to be my colleague?
item.description: The mathematics department has two openings for PhD students in pure mathematics. They are teaching positions, i.e. you have a bigger teaching load than your average PhD student, but to compensate this you get 6 years (3 times 2 years). This also means that you will be required to teach in Dutch the moment you start. Probably that is why there is no English version of the job openings available.
